$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. Every rule here is conditional on the project declaring a design system: a project with strategy 'none-justified' has no tokens to define or use, and these rules report not-applicable with that as the recorded reason rather than passing vacuously.

rules.title: A declared design system defines its primitives
rules.description: Where a project declares a design system, that system defines the primitives it claims to govern — color, spacing, typography, and the others its strategy names.
rules.rationale: A design system that defines nothing is a claim rather than a system, and every consistency argument made on its authority is unfounded.
rules.remediation: Define the primitives in the token source the policy declares, or change the declared strategy to match reality.
rules.$assuranceNote: The declared token paths are read and their definitions counted. Whether the set is complete for the product's needs is a design judgment.

rules.title: Implementations use the tokens that exist
rules.description: Where a token exists for a value, implementations reference it rather than restating the literal, and a feature does not locally redefine a canonical token while claiming to use the system.
rules.rationale: Literals that duplicate tokens are the mechanism by which a design system stops describing the product. Each one is small; the accumulation is what makes a theme change impossible.
rules.remediation: Replace the literal with the token, or add a token if the value is genuinely new.
rules.$assuranceNote: Severity is warning deliberately: the detector fires only where a token system is present, and a literal is sometimes correct. Findings are aggregated per file rather than reported per line, because a per-line report of a drifting file is noise.

rules.title: Breaking token changes are versioned
rules.description: A change that alters or removes an existing token's meaning is released as a versioned change with its consumers named, not applied in place.
rules.rationale: A token is an interface. Changing one silently changes every consumer at once, which is a breaking change delivered without one being declared.
rules.remediation: Version the change, record it, and give consumers a migration path.
rules.$assuranceNote: A changelog entry's presence is checkable. Whether a given change was breaking is a judgment about meaning that no document check makes.

rules.title: Reusable primitives are preferred over repeated local implementations
rules.description: Where a shared component covers an interaction pattern, the pattern is implemented by using it rather than by rebuilding it locally.
rules.rationale: Every local rebuild is a place where accessibility behavior, states, and visual decisions must be gotten right again independently, and where they will drift.
rules.remediation: Adopt the shared component, or extend it where the local case is genuinely different.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether two implementations are the same pattern, and whether consolidating them would produce a better abstraction, is a judgment. interaction.duplicate-component-signals reports the signal; this rule is the decision.

rules.title: A reusable interactive component declares its states
rules.description: A component intended for reuse documents the states it supports, so a consumer knows what is designed and what is not.
rules.rationale: An undocumented state set means every consumer discovers the gaps by shipping them.
rules.remediation: Document the supported states with the component, including which are deliberately absent.
rules.$assuranceNote: Documentation presence is checkable. Whether the documented set matches the component's real behavior is not.

rules.title: Design-system requirements are not weakened for convenience
rules.description: A design-system constraint is not relaxed, an escape hatch is not widened, and a token is not redefined locally, in order to make a particular implementation easier.
rules.rationale: The system's value is entirely in its being binding. Weakening it for the case that finds it inconvenient is how it stops being a system, one exception at a time.
rules.remediation: Solve the case within the system, or change the system deliberately with its consumers considered.
rules.$assuranceNote: A change to the system looks the same whether it was a considered improvement or a convenience. The distinction is intent, established by review.
